summary: Wrecks, busts and a thief leaving all eject the driver before the theft is ended. The eject fires DriverChanged(nil) synchronously, so TheftService.markDropped turns the theft into a 'dropped car' first. It shows Recover/takeover prompts, 'Grab it back!' and 'Get back in!' alerts and a GET BACK IN waypoint, then the theft fails moments later. After a wreck the victim can press the RecoverPrompt on the wrecked car within the 2 s window and collect a recovery bonus.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:1319-1325 wreck() disables the existing prompts, then calls VehicleService.eject(car). eject -> setDriver(car,nil) -> DriverChanged:Fire at line 855. The car is destroyed only after task.delay(WRECK_DESTROY_AFTER=2) at lines 1355-1357. WantedService.luau:413 handleCar runs pcall(VehicleService.eject, car) BEFORE TheftService.fail(car,'busted') at line 417. VehicleService.luau:1684-1688 onPlayerRemoving calls setDriver(car,nil). It is connected in VehicleService.init, before TheftService.init connects its own PlayerRemoving (TheftService.luau:1618), so it runs first. Shared Signal:Fire uses task.spawn, so handlers run immediately. TheftService.luau:1495-1496 onDriverChanged(nil) -> markDropped, lines 868-910: notifies the victim 'was dropped! Grab it back', notifies the thief, sends TheftState dropped=true and adds drop prompts. TheftService.luau:755-774: the RecoverPrompt is created Enabled. Its Triggered handler checks only victim/finished/dropped, never car.wrecked, and calls TheftService.recover. recover (1401-1443) pays _bonus(income, RECOVERY_BONUS_SECONDS) via addCash 'recovery' and posts 'RECOVERED!' plus an EventFeed line. The VehicleService takeover prompt does check car.wrecked (VehicleService.luau:1071); the TheftService RecoverPrompt does not.
failureScenario: Wreck: the victim rams the thief's stolen car to 0 HP. wreck() ejects the thief, markDropped spawns an enabled RecoverPrompt (0.3 s hold) on the burning car, and the victim holds E within 2 s. The victim gets max(100, 30 s of income) bonus and a 'RECOVERED!' feed line, instead of the 'got wrecked... towed home' outcome with no bonus. Bust: the cop busts the thief. In the same frame the victim sees '💥 Your X was dropped! Grab it back in 12s!' and then '🚔 The cops busted the thief!'. The thief also sees 'Get back in!' plus a GET BACK IN waypoint followed by 'Busted!'. A thief leaving the game produces the same contradictory 'dropped' alert.
suggestedFix: End the theft before ejecting. In WantedService.handleCar, call TheftService.fail(car,'busted') before VehicleService.eject (fail already ejects through destroyCar). In VehicleService.wreck, fire Wrecked (or have TheftService listen to Wrecked) before eject, and have TheftService fail thefts with 'wrecked' on that signal. Also have TheftService.onDriverChanged/markDropped return early when car.wrecked or car.destroyed, and make the RecoverPrompt Triggered handler reject car.wrecked. For PlayerRemoving, have markDropped skip players who are leaving, or run TheftService's PlayerRemoving handler before VehicleService's.
verifyReason: Confirmed for wreck and bust. VehicleService.wreck sets car.wrecked, disables the existing prompts, then calls eject. eject -> setDriver(nil) -> DriverChanged:Fire, and Signal.Fire uses task.spawn, so TheftService.onDriverChanged runs immediately. markDropped then creates a brand-new, Enabled RecoverPrompt plus takeover prompt after the disable loop. Nothing in TheftService ends the theft on Wrecked: it listens to Destroyed only, and carAlive only checks model.Parent, so _tick does not catch it either. That leaves the full WRECK_DESTROY_AFTER=2 s window. The RecoverPrompt Triggered handler and TheftService.recover never check car.wrecked, so the victim can hold E for 0.3 s and get the _bonus 'recovery' payout plus a RECOVERED feed line instead of the 'wrecked... towed home' outcome. The VS takeover prompt does reject car.wrecked (line 1071), so takeover is not exploitable. Even with the guard on the signal path, _tick would still call markDropped on a wrecked car after SEAT_GRACE, because driverOf==nil and the model is still parented. So the guard must sit inside markDropped. Bust: WantedService.handleCar calls pcall(eject) before TheftService.fail, so every bust of a thief first sends the victim 'was dropped! Grab it back' and the thief 'Get back in!' plus a GET BACK IN waypoint, then 'busted'. Thief leaving: real only when VehicleService's PlayerRemoving handler runs before TheftService's. Roblox does not guarantee handler order, so the auditor's 'it runs first' claim is not reliable, but the race exists.
fix: 1) src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau, markDropped: at the top add `local car = theft.car; if type(car) == 'table' and (car.wrecked or car.destroyed) then return end`. This covers both the DriverChanged path and the _tick fallback. Destroyed then ends the theft as 'wrecked' 2 s later. 2) Same file, as defense in depth: the RecoverPrompt Triggered handler (and TheftService.recover) should return when `car.wrecked or car.destroyed`. 3) Optional: in TheftService.init connect VS.Wrecked to `failTheft(theft, 'wrecked', true)` (skipDestroy=true so the wreck FX still play) so the theft ends immediately. 4) src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau handleCar: when car.kind == 'Stolen', call TheftService.fail(car, 'busted') BEFORE VehicleService.eject (failTheft finishes first, then destroyCar ejects). Keep the eject for other kinds. 5) For the PlayerRemoving race and the CombatService ordering, TheftService.onDriverChanged could run markDropped via task.defer and re-check `not theft.finished and driverOf(car) == nil` first. Same-dispatch handlers and same-thread follow-ups (fail, onThiefHit) then land before it. Lune tests that call _onDriverChanged synchronously would need a hooks.defer.

summary: When a garage gets laser-locked, PlotService.pushOut moves cars that players are driving with a raw model:PivotTo and zeroes their velocity. It does not use VehicleService.teleport/resetWatchdog, which exist for exactly this kind of server move. The next watchdog pass can then judge the jump a 'teleport', rewind the car back inside the locked garage, take network ownership away for 2 s and log a cheat warning. The velocity zeroing can also trigger crash damage.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1241-1251: for a seated non-owner inside a locked garage, carModel:PivotTo(spot * CFrame.new(0, ride + 0.5, -2)) and primary.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.zero, with no VehicleService call. The spot is at local z = FRONT_Z - 12 = -56 (PlotService.luau:250-254). VehicleService.luau:989-1009 teleport(car, cframe) and resetWatchdog(car) are documented as 'Moves a car on purpose (server teleports) without tripping the watchdog or crash damage'. VehicleService.luau:1561-1575: watchdogPass verdict uses disp > cap*dt + WATCHDOG_TELEPORT_SLACK(10), where cap = topSpeed*1.35*1.3*1.2 (lines 386-392). violate (1500-1530) calls SetNetworkOwner(nil), PivotTo(st.wdCFrame) back to the last valid pose (inside the garage) and warns. damagePass (1437-1457) uses _crashDamage on the sudden velocity drop.
failureScenario: A thief starts stealing slot 11 (local x=-33, z=38) of a 66-studs/s car. The victim, standing inside, hits the LockButton, and lockFor -> pushOut pivots the stolen car about 104 studs to the driveway. The watchdog allowance is about 66*2.1*0.5+10 ≈ 80 studs, so it returns 'teleport'. The car is snapped back to the slot inside the locked garage, the thief loses control for WATCHDOG_REVOKE_SECONDS, the server logs '[VehicleService] watchdog teleport', and pushOut moves it out again 0.5 s later. The car bounces and stalls, and the server logs a false cheat warning on every such lock.
suggestedFix: In pushOut, resolve the car with VehicleService.fromModel(carModel) (lazy sys lookup). Call VehicleService.teleport(car, cf), which pivots and calls resetWatchdog, and zero velocity after that. Fall back to raw PivotTo only when the model is not a registered VehicleService car.
verifyReason: Confirmed. pushOut moves a seated vehicle with a raw carModel:PivotTo and zeroes velocity. No PlotService code calls VehicleService.teleport/resetWatchdog; no system outside VehicleService does. watchdogPass compares flat displacement from st.wdCFrame against cap*dt + WATCHDOG_TELEPORT_SLACK, where cap = topSpeed*1.35*1.3*1.2 and dt ≈ 0.5 s while the car is moving. A 66 top-speed car gets about 79.5 studs. The push target is local (0, FRONT_Z-12 = -56), so back slots (z = 26/38, x = ±33) are 90-100 studs away and get the 'teleport' verdict. violate then revokes ownership, rewinds into the locked garage and warns. Impact is narrower than the auditor says. Only slower cars (top speed below about 95) pushed from rear slots qualify, during the short window when a thief is driving out and the owner locks. It also self-corrects: the next pushOut 0.5 s later moves the car again while the watchdog is revoked, and the revoke delay re-baselines wdCFrame. The result is one bounce, about 2 s of lost control and a false warn. Crash damage is unlikely: the threshold is 55 studs/s of delta-v, and violate sets damage grace.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau pushOut: in the vehicle branch, resolve `local VS = sys('VehicleService'); local car = VS and VS.fromModel and VS.fromModel(carModel)`. Compute the target CFrame as now. When car is found, zero chassis linear and angular velocity first, then call `VS.teleport(car, target)`. teleport pivots and calls resetWatchdog, which re-baselines wdCFrame/wdAt, sets lastVel to the now-zero velocity and grants DAMAGE_GRACE. Otherwise fall back to the current raw PivotTo plus velocity zeroing.

summary: The managed 'Hotwire' prompt on unoccupied Loot cars is hidden from the current claimer only on the client (HideForUserId). The server's canHotwireLoot never rejects the claimer, so the claimer can 'steal' their own loot car again and again. Each time it adds 'steal' contract progress, possibly heat, and a Legendary+ announcement.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:1170-1181 canHotwireLoot checks destroyed/wrecked/kind/driver/Stunned/already-driving only, with no check of car.ownerUserId == player.UserId. VehicleService.luau:1272 setAttr(pp, 'HideForUserId', claimer) is the only gate. Line 1183-1201 hotwireLoot calls addStealHeat, contractProgress(player,'steal',1) and announceSteal on every trigger. Client side, DealershipClient.luau:447-462 applyAudience only sets prompt.Enabled=false locally. The server prompt stays enabled and triggerable (VehicleService.luau:1068-1116 has no audience check). Common/Uncommon wantedOnSteal = 0 (Rarity.luau), so re-stealing costs no heat.
failureScenario: A client that fires the prompt directly (fireproximityprompt), or any client whose audience filter fails to run, keeps exiting and re-hotwiring its own Common loot car. Each trigger counts as a steal and completes the 'Steal 5/12 cars' contracts (300/900 s of income) with zero wanted stars. On Legendary+ cars it spams EventFeed/BigSteal effects.
suggestedFix: In canHotwireLoot, return false (with an 'Use F to get in' message) when car.ownerUserId == player.UserId. Use the EnterPrompt as the claimer's only way back in.
verifyReason: Confirmed. refreshManagedPrompts keeps the Loot 'Hotwire' prompt alive for an idle claimed car, and it hides it from the claimer only through HideForUserId. That is a purely local Enabled=false in DealershipClient.applyAudience. The server Triggered handler in addStealPrompt and canHotwireLoot never compare car.ownerUserId with player.UserId. hotwireLoot then calls addStealHeat (0 stars for Common/Uncommon), contractProgress('steal', 1), which goes into RewardsService.progress with no per-car dedupe, and announceSteal for Legendary+. In normal play the client filter works, so this needs an exploiter firing the prompt (still with a real server-validated hold). It is a server-trust gap with farmable contract progress, so low severity.
fix: src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau canHotwireLoot: after the kind/driver checks, add `if car.ownerUserId == player.UserId then return false, 'Press F to get in!' end`. The claimer's EnterPrompt (onEnterTriggered already allows a Loot claimer) stays their way back in.

summary: VehicleService.seat never throws; it returns (false, reason) on failure. Every caller reads the pcall success flag as 'seated', so all of their seat-failure handling (TheftService's rollback included) is dead code.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:894-976: seat returns false,'gone'/'player'/'not allowed'/'no character'/'occupied'/'sit failed' and never errors. TheftService.luau:160-172: call() returns (pcallOk, firstResult). Line 1190 `local seatOk = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` takes only pcallOk, so the rollback at 1191-1196 (failTheft 'error' + 'The car wouldn't start!') is unreachable. TheftService.luau:971-974 `local seatOk, err = call(...)`; `if not seatOk and err ~= nil` is always false. DealershipService.luau:773-776 and EventService.luau:750-753 have the same pattern. GarageService.luau:938-941 pcall(VS.seat,...) only warns on a throw.
failureScenario: Seat fails during beginTheft, for example 'sit failed' or the thief's character resets between the hold and the seat. The theft is not rolled back: the empty Stolen car sits on the victim's pad, and 2 s later _tick marks it dropped (TheftService.luau:1553-1554). The victim gets a 'dropped' alarm, a victim cooldown starts, and the thief still gets heat and 'steal' contract progress, instead of the intended clean restore.
suggestedFix: Read the second return value: `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` and then `if not (okCall and seated == true) then ...`. Apply the same change in takeover, DealershipService.onSteal, EventService.claimHotDrop and GarageService.driveSlot. GarageService can roll back with ps.states[slot]='Parked' + destroy; Dealership/HotDrop can fall back to the claim prompt.
verifyReason: Confirmed as a code defect. VehicleService.seat returns (false, reason) and does not throw. TheftService/DealershipService/EventService `call` helpers return (pcallOk, firstResult), and GarageService uses raw pcall, so every `seatOk` is the pcall flag. The TheftService.beginTheft rollback is unreachable, and the takeover warn condition `not seatOk and err ~= nil` can never be true. Real-world impact is lower than the auditor claims. beginTheft runs gatherState (alive, not driving, etc.) synchronously right before seat, and VS.spawn has no yields, so 'the thief's character resets between the hold and the seat' cannot happen. In practice only a seat:Sit pcall error ('sit failed') reaches the bad path. That path then degrades to the dropped-car flow (_tick marks it dropped after SEAT_GRACE), which also lets the victim instant-recover for a bonus. Dealership/EventService/GarageService only lose a warn; GarageService's car stays as an Owned car with an EnterPrompt, which is acceptable.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau beginTheft: `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService', 'seat', car, thief); if not okCall or seated ~= true then failTheft(theft, 'error'); notify(...); return false end`. In takeover, use `local okCall, seated = call(...); if not okCall or seated ~= true then warn(...) end` (the drop timer self-heals after SEAT_GRACE). Optionally apply the same second-value read in DealershipService.onSteal and EventService.claimHotDrop (warn only). In GarageService.driveSlot use `local okP, seated, why = pcall(VS.seat, car, player)` for logging. No rollback is needed there because the owner can press F.

summary: CombatService ejects the thief before it calls TheftService.onThiefHit. markDropped runs synchronously inside the eject, so theft.lastHitBy/lastHitAt are not yet set, and the 'X knocked Y out of Z's car!' EventFeed never fires on the first knockout of a theft.
evidence: CombatService.luau:879-885: stun(victim) -> callSystem('VehicleService','eject',car) -> ... -> callSystem('TheftService','onThiefHit',attacker,victim). The eject fires DriverChanged synchronously, and TheftService.luau:1495-1496 runs markDropped immediately. TheftService.luau:900-908 posts the knockout EventFeed only if `hitter and now - theft.lastHitAt <= KNOCKOUT_WINDOW`, and those fields are written later by onThiefHit (1466-1468). The drop timer itself is still correct because the Stunned attribute is set first (873-876).
failureScenario: A victim bonks the thief out of their stolen car. The car drops, but the server-wide '🔨 Victim knocked Thief out of ...' feed line is skipped. It only appears if the same thief was already hit earlier in that theft.
suggestedFix: In CombatService.applyHit, call TheftService.onThiefHit(attacker, victim) before VehicleService.eject. Alternatively, have markDropped re-check for a hit 1 frame later (task.defer) before posting the feed.
verifyReason: Confirmed. In CombatService.applyHit the order is stun (sets the Stunned attribute synchronously), then callSystem VehicleService.eject, then TheftService.onThiefHit. eject -> setDriver(nil) -> DriverChanged:Fire (task.spawn runs immediately) -> markDropped. At that point theft.lastHitBy is nil and lastHitAt is -inf on the first hit, so the `hitter and now - lastHitAt <= KNOCKOUT_WINDOW` EventFeed branch is skipped. The drop timer is still right, because knocked is true via the Stunned attribute. This only costs a cosmetic server-wide feed line.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau applyHit: move `callSystem('TheftService', 'onThiefHit', attacker, victim)` above the `if car then callSystem('VehicleService', 'eject', car) end` block. onThiefHit does not depend on the eject, and `defended` and `heat` are already computed beforehand.

summary: AssetLibrary loads and publishes about 110 templates to ReplicatedStorage, but nothing consumes them. The slot roles MapBuilder writes do not match any Assets key, so wiring a swapper later would still find nothing.
evidence: AssetLibrary.luau:269-288 get/clone have no callers; a grep of src finds AssetLibrary referenced only in init.server.luau ORDER. VehicleService.luau:616 builds every car with CarBuilder.buildDef only, so Assets.Hero shells are never applied (also noted in vehicles-world.md). MapBuilder.luau:498 uses role 'palm_tree', line 526 'tree', line 600 'building_'..lower(class). Assets.luau:64-117 Props keys are palm_tree_a / palm_tree_b / round_tree / pine_tree, and lines 121-142 Buildings keys carry no 'building_' prefix (apartment_balcony, office_block, ...).
failureScenario: Every server spends boot time loading all hero, prop and building assets and replicates the normalized templates (skyscrapers up to 240 studs) to every client, and none of them is ever shown. A future AssetSlot swapper keyed on Role would still fall back to procedural geometry for every tree and building because the keys don't match.
suggestedFix: Either wire the consumers (VehicleService.spawn / CarBuilder hero shell by carId; an AssetSlot swapper that maps Role -> Assets key) and align the names, for example Role 'palm_tree' -> {'palm_tree_a','palm_tree_b'} and 'building_<class>' -> the class key. Or keep templates in ServerStorage until a consumer exists, so they don't replicate.
verifyReason: Confirmed as stated. AssetLibrary.start loads 108 entries (Hero + Props + Buildings) and publishes them under ReplicatedStorage, so they replicate to every client. It runs in start, so boot is not blocked. A grep of src finds no reader of AssetLibrary.get/clone, no ReplicatedStorage.AssetLibrary lookup and no Hero use in CarBuilder, and the MapDresser named in docs/ART_PASS.md does not exist. Roles also do not equal keys: MapBuilder writes 'palm_tree', 'tree' and 'building_'..lower(class) for the classes Tower, Midrise, Shop, House, PoliceHQ and Landmark. The Props keys are palm_tree_a/_b, round_tree and pine_tree, and no Buildings key matches even with the prefix stripped (for example 'policehq' vs 'police_hq'). However, this is the documented, not-yet-done art pass: vehicles-world.md:321 notes the hero shells are not applied, and ART_PASS.md says MapDresser picks 'variants... deterministically by position', which implies a role-to-variants table rather than equal names. So this is wasted load and replication today plus a latent naming gap, not a live gameplay bug.
fix: When doing the art pass, add src/server/Systems/MapDresser.luau with an explicit ROLE_VARIANTS table, for example palm_tree -> {palm_tree_a, palm_tree_b}, tree -> {round_tree, pine_tree}, building_tower -> {skyscraper_deco, skyscraper_neon, skyscraper_twist, office_block}, building_midrise -> {apartment_balcony, brick_loft, office_block}, building_shop -> {convenience_store, diner, donut_shop, pizza_shop}, building_house -> {suburban_house, beach_villa}, building_policehq -> {police_hq}. Also add the hero-shell hookup after CarBuilder.buildDef in VehicleService.spawn. Until then, gate AssetLibrary.start behind a config flag (for example Assets.ENABLED = false) or drop it from ORDER in src/server/init.server.luau, so clients don't download unused templates.

summary: The Rebirth remote is registered with a rate limit of 0.5/s. Net's token bucket starts at `perSecond` tokens and needs at least 1 token, so the server silently drops the first Rebirth request from every player in every server session.
evidence: RebirthService.luau:303-305 registers `Net.on("Rebirth", function(player) RebirthService.rebirth(player) end, 0.5)`. Net.luau:100 creates the bucket as `b = { tokens = perSecond, last = now }`, i.e. 0.5 tokens. Line 103 refills it with `b.tokens = math.min(perSecond * 2, b.tokens + (now - b.last) * perSecond)`, which leaves 0.5 on the first call, and line 105 returns false via `if b.tokens < 1 then return false end`. On the client, MenuController.luau:2812-2817 fires `Net.fire("Rebirth")` exactly once, after the second confirm tap, then sets `pendingUntil = now + PENDING_SECONDS` (3s, line 75). Every other Net.on handler uses a rate of 1 or more, so Rebirth is the only one affected. AdminService's `rebirth` command is not affected because it calls RebirthService.rebirth directly.
failureScenario: A player with enough cash opens the Rebirth menu and taps REBIRTH twice to confirm. The first-ever Rebirth remote of their session reaches Net.allow with 0.5 tokens and is discarded before RebirthService runs. The server sends no Notify. The button shows 'REBIRTHING...' for 3s, then re-enables with nothing changed. The player has to confirm again at least 1s later for the rebirth to happen, and this repeats on every new server.
suggestedFix: Register the Rebirth handler with a rate of at least 1; RebirthService's `busy` guard and the cash check already stop double rebirths. Alternatively, change Net.allow to seed new buckets with `math.max(1, perSecond)` tokens, so any rate below 1 still lets the first call through.
verifyReason: Confirmed. src/shared/Net.luau allow() creates a new bucket with `tokens = perSecond` (0.5) and caps refills at `perSecond * 2` (1). On the first call almost no time has passed, so tokens stay at 0.5, which is below 1, and allow returns false. Net.on then drops the event before RebirthService runs. RebirthService.init registers `Net.on("Rebirth", ..., 0.5)` (RebirthService.luau:303-305). It is the only server Net.on/Net.handle with a rate below 1. Nothing else calls allow() for "Rebirth" beforehand, and the client fires it in one place only (MenuController.luau:2817, after the confirm tap). The button then waits PENDING_SECONDS=3. A retry after that has 0.5+1.5 tokens, capped at 1, so it goes through. Net: the first confirmed rebirth of every player in every server is silently ignored with no toast. No data is lost, but this is the core progression action and it looks broken, so medium fits.
fix: src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau:305: change the rate from 0.5 to 1. RebirthService.rebirth already guards against double rebirths with `busy[player]` plus the cash check. Optional hardening in src/shared/Net.luau allow(): seed new buckets with `tokens = math.max(1, perSecond)` and cap with `math.max(1, perSecond * 2)`, so any sub-1 rate still lets the first call through.

summary: The built-in `clear_wanted` product handler reports a successful grant whenever WantedService.clear runs without throwing, even when the player has no stars. A player can therefore be charged Robux for 'Lose the Cops' and get nothing.
evidence: MonetizationService.luau:341-349 does `local ok = callSystem("WantedService", "clear", player, "purchase")` and returns true when `ok`, where `ok` is only pcall success. WantedService.luau:349-355 shows `clear` silently returns when `not st or st.stars == 0` and returns no status. processWhileLocked (MonetizationService.luau:442-458) then records the receipt and returns PurchaseGranted. MenuController.luau contains no reference to `clear_wanted` or `Wanted`, so the client store never disables the product while the player has 0 stars.
failureScenario: Once the product id is set, a player with Wanted=0 opens the Store and buys 'Lose the Cops'. ProcessReceipt runs the handler, clear() does nothing, and the handler returns true. The receipt is saved, the purchase is granted (Robux charged), and the player gets a 'You're clean!' toast for no effect.
suggestedFix: In the clear_wanted handler, check `WantedService.getStars(player) > 0` and return false otherwise, so the receipt stays NotProcessedYet. Also hide or disable the product in MenuController's Store while the Wanted attribute is 0.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The clear_wanted handler (MonetizationService.luau:341-349) checks only the pcall status from callSystem (lines 111-121 return pcall(fn, ...)). WantedService.clear (WantedService.luau:349-355) returns nothing and does nothing when `not st or st.stars == 0`. processWhileLocked therefore records the receipt and returns PurchaseGranted, and the player sees 'You're clean!'. Client side, MenuController.storeItems (559-592) lists every product with id > 0, and refreshStore (1464-1480) always enables the buy button, with no Wanted check. HUDController has no separate Lose-the-Cops entry point. Today the product id is 0 in Monetization.luau, so this is not live yet. Once the id is configured, a player with 0 stars can pay Robux for nothing. The same happens if their stars decay between the prompt and receipt processing. This contradicts economy-server.md:46 ('never charged for nothing').
fix: 1) src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau, clear_wanted handler: before clearing, do `local okS, stars = callSystem("WantedService", "getStars", player); if not okS or typeof(stars) ~= "number" or stars <= 0 then return false end`, then call clear and return true. Returning false keeps the receipt NotProcessedYet, so it is not granted. 2) Prevent the prompt in the first place, in src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau refreshStore. For the item with key == "clear_wanted", when `(player:GetAttribute("Wanted") or 0) <= 0`, show 'NOT WANTED' and disable the button with setButton(..., false). Also have promptPurchase refuse in that case. Refresh on Wanted attribute changes while the Store is open.

summary: AdminService treats 'the call did not throw' as 'the command succeeded'. Several of the functions it wires to report failure through their return value instead, so admins get success messages for commands that did nothing.
evidence: AdminService.luau:194-210: callFirst returns `true, name.."."..fnName` whenever `pcall(fn, ...)` succeeds and ignores the function's results. Used at :423-426 (hotdrop/event) and :456-458 (rebirth). At :360-364, `okSeat` is only pcall success. The targets that return a failure status are: RebirthService.rebirth at RebirthService.luau:226-247, which returns `false, "cash"|"blocked"|"busy"`; EventService.startHotDrop at EventService.luau:969-972, which returns false if a drop is already running; EventService.startCashRain at EventService.luau:1166-1170, which returns false if one is already running; and VehicleService.seat at VehicleService.luau:894-918, which returns `false, reason` and never throws.
failureScenario: `/hc rebirth` while a garage car is out driving: RebirthService refuses with 'Park your car back...', but the admin also gets 'Rebirthed via RebirthService.rebirth'. `/hc hotdrop` during an active drop reports 'hotDrop started via EventService.forceHotDrop' although nothing started. `/hc spawn` reports 'drive it home' even when seat() returned (false, 'no character').
suggestedFix: Have callFirst and callSystem check the first return value: treat `ok and result ~= false` as success and include the second return value (the reason) in the message. Do the same for the seat result in the `spawn` command.
verifyReason: Confirmed with one correction. callFirst (AdminService.luau:193-209) returns `true, name.."."..fnName` whenever pcall succeeds and discards the function's return values. EventService has no forceHotDrop, so hotdrop resolves to startHotDrop. That function returns false while a drop is active or when there are no points (EventService.luau:969-976). The admin sees 'hotDrop started via EventService.startHotDrop', not forceHotDrop as the auditor wrote. startCashRain (1166-1170) returns false while one is running, with the same false success. The rebirth command calls RebirthService.rebirth, which returns false with 'busy', 'blocked', 'cash' or 'loading', and the admin still gets 'Rebirthed via RebirthService.rebirth'. RebirthService does also send its own error Notify. In spawn, `local okSeat, err = callSystem("VehicleService", "seat", ...)` binds err to the boolean result. When seat returns (false, "no character"/"occupied"/...), okSeat is true and the admin gets 'drive it home'. This is admin-only messaging with no gameplay or data impact, so low.
fix: src/server/Systems/AdminService.luau only. In callFirst, replace `local ok, err = pcall(fn, ...)` with `local ok, res, why = pcall(fn, ...)`. If ok and res ~= false, return true with name..'.'..fnName. If ok and res == false, return false with ('%s.%s refused: %s'):format(name, fnName, tostring(why or 'already running')). The pcall-error branch stays as is. In the rebirth command, when callFirst fails because of a refusal, return false with the reason instead of the generic 'Cash topped up' success. In spawn, use `local okSeat, seated, why = callSystem("VehicleService", "seat", car, player)` and treat `not okSeat or seated ~= true` as 'could not seat you: '..tostring(if okSeat then why else seated).

summary: The rebirth luck bonus is advertised to players but no server code applies it. Every rarity roll uses only the server-wide EventService.getLuck(), which ignores the player's rebirths.
evidence: Economy.luau:120 defines `REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS = 0.1`. MenuController.luau:2737 shows '+{REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS*100}% rare car luck (every rebirth)' in the Rebirth menu, and the RebirthService.luau:2 header claims a 'permanent +50% income (and luck) multiplier'. A search of src/server finds no use of REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS. The luck consumers are StreetSpawnService.luau:97, DealershipService.luau:541 and TrafficService.luau:785, and all of them call EventService.getLuck(). That function (EventService.luau:523-525) only combines serverLuck and rushHour timers.
failureScenario: A player rebirths expecting +10% rare-car luck per rebirth, as the menu promises. Their street, traffic, dealer and hot-drop rolls are exactly the same as a player with 0 rebirths.
suggestedFix: Either apply the bonus where a roll is attributable to a player (e.g. a per-player luck factor of `1 + rebirths * REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS` in the newbie/street rolls near that player, or in dealer stock rolls), or remove the luck line from the Rebirth menu and the RebirthService header.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS = 0.1 (Economy.luau:120) is referenced only by the client Rebirth menu (MenuController.luau:2737, '+10% rare car luck (every rebirth)'). No server file reads it. Every rarity roll gets its luck from EventService.getLuck(), which combines only serverLuck and rushHour: StreetSpawnService.luau:96-101/284, DealershipService.luau:540-545, TrafficService.luau:785, and the hot drop roll. The RebirthService.luau:2 header also claims '(and luck)'. SPEC §RebirthService does not require a luck bonus, so the defect is a reward that is advertised but never granted. Income, the main reward, works, so low.
fix: Minimal and correct: remove the false promise. Delete the '🍀 +X% rare car luck' segment from the bodyLabel at src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau:2737, leaving '🔒 +10s garage lock (every rebirth)'. Drop '(and luck)' from the src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau header, and remove or mark the unused Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS. Implementing it properly needs per-player rolls, which the world spawners do not have. The only player-attributable roll is StreetSpawnService's newbie spawn (entry.newbieFor). That would mean multiplying luck there by `1 + rebirths * REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS`, a design change rather than a bug fix.

summary: MapBuilder builds a tagged `DealerRestockBoard` (its comment says 'DealershipService draws on it') and tagged `DealerPad` discs with neon rims. DealershipService never looks up either tag and builds its own RestockSign and Turntable/Rim parts at the same spots. The result is a blank duplicate board behind the real sign, doubled pad discs and rims, and the real sign cutting into MapBuilder's canopy.
evidence: MapBuilder.luau:1376-1383 builds `DealerPad<i>` (20 dia, tagged "DealerPad") plus a neon `DealerPadRim` (21.4 dia) at MapLayout.dealerPads(). MapBuilder.luau:1448-1457 builds the "RestockBoard" (18x6 at o+(0,11,45.2), tagged "DealerRestockBoard") and a Canopy slab at y 18.8±0.8 spanning z≈34.5..48.5 (line 1404). DealershipService.luau:1041-1065 only raycasts Workspace.Map for floor height, then calls buildShowroom (431-470). That creates its own Turntable<i> with a neon Rim (d+1.4) and a RestockSign at center+(0,0,41) (SIGN_OFFSET, line 47), with bottom at floor+9 and size 34x10 (lines 48-49). Neither tag is referenced anywhere in DealershipService.
failureScenario: In-game, a plain dark 18x6 board stands 4 studs behind the real countdown sign. Two neon rims overlap under every turntable. The real sign spans about floor+9..19.5, which overlaps the canopy (≈18.6..20.2 at z≈41), so its top frame is buried in the roof.
suggestedFix: Pick one owner for these parts. Either have DealershipService attach its SurfaceGui to the part tagged DealerRestockBoard and reuse the DealerPad discs, or remove the RestockBoard and pad/rim parts from MapBuilder. In either case, lower SIGN_BOTTOM or SIGN_SIZE so the sign clears the canopy.
verifyReason: Partly refuted, partly confirmed. That DealershipService ignores the DealerPad and DealerRestockBoard tags is not a contract violation in itself: vehicles-world.md:215 says DealershipService 'may use them but don't have to'. The functional effect is benign. floorAt raycasts down onto MapBuilder's queryable DealerPad (top at CURB_TOP+0.2), so the turntables simply sit on it. The doubled same-colour rims (21.4 at floor, 20.4 on top) read as a stepped ring, which is cosmetic. MapBuilder's 18x6 RestockBoard at z+45.2, y 8..14 is almost entirely hidden behind the 34x10 DS sign, with a sliver showing below it and its back visible through the rear glass. The real, confirmed defect is headroom. economy-server.md:214 says the sign needs 19 studs of headroom, but MapBuilder's back Canopy (L(o,0,18.8,41.5), 1.6 tall, z 34.5..48.5) has its underside at CURB_TOP+18.0. The DS sign floor is CURB_TOP+0.2 (raycast onto pad 1), so the board spans +9.2..+19.2 and the top neon frame +19.2..+19.7, at z≈40.5..41.5. The top 1.2 studs of the board and the whole top frame are buried inside the canopy slab, and the frame pokes 0.1 above the roof. The SurfaceGui Title occupies the top 3-30% of the board (≈+16.2..+18.9), so its upper ~0.9 studs are hidden.
fix: src/server/Systems/DealershipService.luau: lower the sign so it clears the canopy underside (CURB_TOP+18.0) and the LightPanel (bottom +17.7). For example, set SIGN_BOTTOM = 7 (board +7.2..+17.2, frame top +17.7), or keep SIGN_BOTTOM=9 and set SIGN_SIZE = Vector3.new(34, 8, 0.8). Optional cleanup to remove the duplicates: delete the RestockBoard part, and if wanted the DealerPad/DealerPadRim discs, from buildDealership in src/server/Systems/MapBuilder.luau (lines ~1375-1383 and 1447-1457), and update vehicles-world.md. Alternatively, have DealershipService.buildShowroom skip its own Rim when a DealerPad-tagged part exists. If the MapBuilder pads are removed, floorYs drops by 0.2 automatically through the raycast.

summary: When a player joins, GarageClient hides the StealPrompt on every display car that already exists. At that moment its plot views are still empty, so it reads the victim's CarCount as 0, and nothing recomputes the prompt once the views are built.
evidence:
Client side:
- GarageClient.start (GarageClient.luau:709-713) runs setupDisplay for every tagged DisplayCar before the Workspace.Plots views are built. The plots are only processed later, inside task.spawn (719-731).
- setupDisplay's task.spawn calls WaitForChild("Chassis",5) (320). That returns without yielding when Chassis exists, so updatePrompts(model) runs at once (325).
- updatePrompts (136-139) does `views[PlotIndex]`, which is nil, so `cars = 0` and `steal.Enabled = ... and cars >= Economy.NEWBIE_PROTECTION_CARS` sets the prompt to false.
- setupPlot (595-643) registers the view and calls applyGate/renderPads but never updatePlotPrompts(view).
- The only later re-evaluations are: the plot's CarCount/Locked attributes changing (624-631), the local Driving/HoldMultiplier attributes changing (716-717), or PlotIndex changing (715).

Server side:
- The server never re-enables the prompt and relies on the client for this. GarageService creates StealPrompt enabled and never touches .Enabled (GarageService.luau:548-551).
- CarCount is only re-set when the pad key changes (600-616).
- PlotIndex is set in PlotService.assign on PlayerAdded (PlotService.luau:1420), before client controllers start, so no change event reaches the client.
- Driving is first written only when the player first sits in a car (VehicleService.luau:806/817).
- HoldMultiplier is only written when its value changes (VehicleService.luau:479-480).
failureScenario:
1. Player B joins a server where A already has 5 cars parked.
2. B walks into A's garage on foot. No 'Steal' prompt appears on any of A's cars, because the client disabled it locally with cars=0.
3. It stays hidden until B drives some car and gets out (the Driving true→false flip calls updateAllPrompts), or A buys/loses a car or locks the garage.
The core 'rob a player garage' loop is invisible to fresh joiners and returning players who go straight to a garage on foot.
suggestedFix: Call updatePlotPrompts(view) (or updateAllPrompts()) at the end of setupPlot. As an alternative or in addition, have updatePrompts return without changing Enabled when the view is nil, and re-run it once views exist. The cheapest fix is `updatePlotPrompts(view)` right after `renderPads(view)` in setupPlot.
verifyReason:
Confirmed by reading the code. In GarageClient.start (GarageClient.luau:709-713), setupDisplay runs synchronously for every DisplayCar that already exists. Its task.spawn body runs immediately: WaitForChild('Chassis',5) does not yield when Chassis is present, and buildBillboard has no yields. So updatePrompts(model) (line 325) runs while `views` is still empty, because the Plots loop is spawned later at 719-731. view is nil, so cars is 0, which is below Economy.NEWBIE_PROTECTION_CARS (3), and steal.Enabled is set false locally. setupPlot (595-643) never calls updatePlotPrompts/updateAllPrompts.

I found no other recompute:
- syncOwnership is only wired to the player's PlotIndex change and the plot's OwnerUserId change. Both are set inside PlotService.assign during the server's PlayerAdded (PlotService.luau:1407-1424, 1580), normally before client start.
- The server never touches StealPrompt.Enabled; makePrompt (GarageService.luau:438-461) leaves the default true.
- SetAttribute('CarCount', same value) in updatePads fires no change event.
- Driving is only written by VehicleService.luau:806/817.
- HoldMultiplier is only written on change (VehicleService.luau:479). It is 1 at PlayerAdded and only changes later for players with the hotwire upgrade or pass.
- StreamingEnabled=false (default.project.json:36), and the client bootstrap (init.client.luau) does not wait for game.Loaded, so the display cars are normally present at start.

Mitigation: the prompt reappears the first time the player sits in or leaves any car (the Driving flip calls updateAllPrompts), and most fresh players steal a street car first. That keeps this at medium rather than high: a returning player who walks straight into a garage cannot rob it.
fix: In src/client/Controllers/GarageClient.luau, in setupPlot, add `updatePlotPrompts(view)` right after `renderPads(view)` (before the collectFx check). This re-evaluates every display car under that plot's Display folder once the view is registered. It covers both orders: display before plot, now fixed, and plot before display, already fine. No server change is needed.

summary: TheftService sends the thief's dropped-car state (dropped, droppedEndsAt) in TheftState. StateController.sanitizeTheft silently strips those fields, so the HUD keeps showing the long delivery countdown while the real deadline is the 12-20 s dropped-car timer.
evidence:
- Server: TheftService.sendThiefState (TheftService.luau:534-548) fires TheftState {active, endsAt, carId, mutation, targetPlot, victimName, dropped, droppedEndsAt}. It is re-sent when the car is dropped or retaken (898, 918, 977). The drop deadline is _dropTimeout = DROPPED_CAR_TIMEOUT or THEFT_ABANDON_LIMIT (356-358).
- Client: the StateController TheftState type (StateController.luau:29) and sanitizeTheft (86-96) keep only active/endsAt/carId/targetPlot.
- HUDController.applyTheft (HUDController.luau:1303-1308) and refreshTheft (1330) can therefore only render endsAt.
failureScenario:
1. A thief is bonked out of the stolen car.
2. The server marks it dropped, with the car returning to the victim in 12-20 s.
3. The thief's HUD still shows e.g. '1:40' remaining and gives no 'GET BACK IN' urgency. The car is towed home 'unexpectedly'; the only cue is the waypoint label.
suggestedFix: Add `dropped: boolean?` and `droppedEndsAt: number?` (plus mutation and victimName if wanted) to StateController.TheftState and sanitizeTheft. In HUDController.applyTheft/refreshTheft, show droppedEndsAt with a 'GET BACK IN!' style when dropped == true.
verifyReason:
Confirmed.
- TheftService.sendThiefState (TheftService.luau:534-548) sends dropped and droppedEndsAt, re-sent from markDropped (898) and the retake/takeover paths (918, 977).
- StateController.TheftState (StateController.luau:29) and sanitizeTheft (86-96) keep only active/endsAt/carId/targetPlot.
- HUDController receives state only through StateController.TheftChanged/getTheft (1821-1824).
- applyTheft (1303-1321) and refreshTheft (1330) use only endsAt with THEFT_TOTAL=150.
- No client code reads the car's DroppedEndsAt attribute either.
The integration notes already list this gap (docs/integration/gameplay-client.md:334). Impact is UX only: the thief does get a 4 s toast 'Get back in! The car gets towed in Ns!' and a 'GET BACK IN!' waypoint, so 'unexpectedly' overstates it. Server logic is correct. Low is the right rating.
fix:
1. src/client/Controllers/StateController.luau: extend the TheftState type with `dropped: boolean?, droppedEndsAt: number?`. In sanitizeTheft, add `dropped = raw.dropped == true` and `droppedEndsAt = if typeof(raw.droppedEndsAt) == 'number' and raw.droppedEndsAt == raw.droppedEndsAt then raw.droppedEndsAt else nil`.
2. src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau, in applyTheft: when `state.dropped == true` and droppedEndsAt is a number, set theftEndsAt = state.droppedEndsAt, set a module-level theftTotal = Economy.DROPPED_CAR_TIMEOUT, and set u.theftTitle.Text to '🚨 GET BACK IN!'. Otherwise use endsAt, THEFT_TOTAL and '🚨 DELIVER IT HOME!'. Reset theftLastSecond when the dropped flag flips.
3. In refreshTheft, pass theftTotal instead of THEFT_TOTAL to theftView. THEFT_URGENT=20 already makes a 12-20 s drop timer show red and pulse.

summary: PoliceService turns sirens off through the model attribute Siren=false when units leave or are wrecked, but no client reads that attribute. Sirens keep wailing and lights keep flashing on retreating or wrecked cruisers.
evidence:
- Server: PoliceService sets the Siren attribute in sendAway (PoliceService.luau:751, false), markWrecked (766, false), spawnUnit (931, true) and on rejoin (1931, true).
- Client: `grep '"Siren"' src/client` finds only sound keys and a GUI name. There are no GetAttribute("Siren") reads.
- SoundController's siren slot selection (SoundController.luau:619-634) picks any Police-tagged model within range.
- EffectsController.updateSirens (EffectsController.luau:1465-1495) flashes SirenRed/SirenBlue and the PointLight on any Police-tagged model, with no attribute check.
failureScenario:
1. A player escapes at decay and gets the 'ESCAPED!' feedback.
2. Their stars go to 0 and the units switch to 'leaving' with Siren=false.
3. For up to about 15 s (until despawn), cruisers around them still blare the siren loop and flash red/blue. Wrecked cruisers also keep flashing and wailing for the 6 s before replacement.
suggestedFix: In SoundController's siren candidate loop and EffectsController.updateSirens, skip models where `model:GetAttribute("Siren") == false`. For EffectsController, reset part transparency and disable the flash light for those models.
verifyReason:
Confirmed. PoliceService sets the model attribute Siren=false in sendAway (PoliceService.luau:752) and markWrecked (766), and true in spawnUnit (931) and on rejoin (1931). No client code calls GetAttribute('Siren'); the only 'Siren' strings in src/client are sound keys and a GUI name.
- SoundController's siren candidate loop (SoundController.luau:619-633) takes any tracked Police-tagged model within SIREN_RANGE.
- EffectsController.updateSirens (~1465-1495) flashes SirenRed/SirenBlue and the PointLight for any Police-tagged model in range.
- The Police tag is only removed through VehicleService.setKind (VehicleService.luau:711), which is not used on leave or wreck.
The docs state the intent: 'Units leave (sirens off, routed away)' in gameplay-client.md:146.

Two timing details are off in the report:
- Wrecked units are cleaned up after WRECK_CLEANUP_AFTER = 4 s, not 6 (6 is WRECK_RESPAWN_DELAY).
- Leaving units despawn 3 s after leaving once no player is within 140 studs, so the full 15 s (LEAVE_TIME 3 + LEAVE_MAX_TIME 12) applies only while a player stays close.
This is a cosmetic and audio mismatch, so low is the right rating.
fix:
1. src/client/Controllers/SoundController.luau, siren candidate loop (~line 619): after the Parent check, add `if model:GetAttribute('Siren') == false then continue end`. selectNearest/distribute then releases that model's slot.
2. src/client/Controllers/EffectsController.luau, updateSirens: after the `not model.Parent` cleanup, add the check below. Flashing resumes automatically when the server sets Siren=true on rejoin.
```
if model:GetAttribute('Siren') == false then
  for _, p in rec.reds do p.Transparency = 0.8 end
  for _, p in rec.blues do p.Transparency = 0.8 end
  if rec.light then rec.light.Enabled = false end
  continue
end
```
Any steady 'off' transparency works. Treat nil as on, so units spawned before the attribute replicates still flash.
